steps.action: OpenLaw checks the account's actual role, whichever sign-in page the person opened
steps.expected: With Legal password sign-in off, a Legal Team Member is refused on the Portal page too; a Business User with a password can use the staff page
steps.actual: With Email and password off under Legal User Authentication, the Legal Team Member's password sign-in on the Business Portal page was refused (Password sign-in is disabled for this account.; me 401). With Business Portal password sign-in on, the Business User's password sign-in on the staff page succeeded (me 200, business_user, landed /portal/onboarding). Legal password sign-in was turned back on.

steps.action: An identity with no account is refused when it first redeems a link issued before its domain was removed
steps.actual: A never-seen address on northwind.example got "Sign in to OpenLaw" while the domain was allowed. After Remove northwind.example, opening that link ended on /api/auth/magic-link/verify ("{"message":"This email address is not eligible for portal access."}") with no session (me 401) and no account. The domain was added back.
